subject: PineBridge SLA template — monthly credit cap and regional split request
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@pinebridge.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@pinebridge.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template — initial ask on monthly cap and regional split

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks great. Procurement asked us to get a straighter line on two SLA items before we can move to internal approval:

1) Monthly credit cap: we need to understand your willingness to limit monthly service credit exposure. For budgeting reasons we prefer an absolute cap on credits (percent of monthly invoice or fixed amount). Can Redwood propose a standard cap and a path for exceptions?

2) Regional split: our service footprint is US + EU. We want credits to be allocated regionally (i.e., outages in EU only reduce EU region availability and credits). Does your template support per-region accounting, or is it global by default?

Also — our security/compliance team requests a maintenance carve-out definition (scheduled windows and advance notice). If you can attach your SLA template and a simple monthly-credit schedule we can circulate.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — internal review on Thursday.

Best,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Procurement
PineBridge Analytics

Attachments: none in this message
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@pinebridge.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template — initial ask on monthly cap and regional split

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together our standard SLA template and a simple credit schedule (attached). High level answers below and then a proposed path if you need narrower terms: 

• Monthly credit cap: Our standard template caps monthly credits at 30% of the monthly invoice for the affected service. We can consider a lower cap (down to 20%) with a 12‑month committed reserved capacity addendum — that’s our usual commercial tradeoff.

• Regional accounting: The template supports per-region availability measurement. By default we report both per-region and global metrics, and credits are applied only to the affected region’s bill unless you request blended billing treatment.

• Maintenance carve-out: Our standard carve-out is scheduled maintenance windows announced 72 hours in advance, limited to a cumulative 6 hours per month per region. Emergency maintenance is excluded but only applied with post-event notice and root cause. We can tighten the notice to 96 hours for EU if that helps.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review attached SLA_Template_v2_redlines.pdf for the default wording.
2) I’ve included a draft Monthly_Credit_Schedule_PineBridge.xlsx that shows 99.95% uptime = 0% credits, 99.90–99.95 = 10% credit, 99.50–99.90 = 25%, below 99.50 = 50% (these apply to the affected region).
3) If you want a lower absolute cap, tell us the target and I’ll run it by finance for a committed capacity passthrough.

If you’re comfortable, I can send a version with the 20% cap language and a short commercial addendum for the committed capacity.

I’ll wait to hear where procurement wants to land.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0124

Attachments: SLA_Template_v2_redlines.pdf; Monthly_Credit_Schedule_PineBridge.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fw: SLA template — internal notes on concession room

Marissa / Logan — internal quick note before we respond to Jordan.

Notes:
• Credit cap: Finance will accept a 25% monthly credit cap if PineBridge signs a 12‑month reserved capacity commitment at a minimum $50k/mo ARR equivalent. Anything below that and margin goes negative in our model.
• Maintenance carve-out: We can reduce monthly carve-out to 4 hours for EU only (96 hr notice) but need to keep 6 hours for US due to multi-cluster patching windows.
• Regional split: Approved — we can instrument per-region telemetry and bill credits regionally; engineering asks we agree on a single canonical region list in the SOW to avoid ambiguity.
• Reporting cadence: propose monthly availability report and a 10‑day SLA dispute window.

Action items for Marissa: propose the 25% cap + 12m commitment option and offer a fall-back of 30% w/o commitment. Also confirm we provide the canonical region list in the SOW.

Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

(Internal only — do not include outside the org)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@pinebridge.ai>
Cc: procurement@pinebridge.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template — monthly credit cap and regional split request

Jordan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Based on internal alignment we can offer two paths and we included both in the attached redline and a short commercial addendum: 

Option A (preferred for budget predictability):
• Monthly credit cap: 25% of the affected region’s monthly invoice.
• Commitment: requires a 12‑month reserved capacity commitment (minimum $50k/mo).

Option B (standard):
• Monthly credit cap: 30% of the affected region’s monthly invoice.
• No reserved capacity requirement.

Regional accounting: credits applied per-region by default; we will include the canonical region list in the SOW (US, EU‑west, and APAC as defined in the SOW) and provide monthly per-region availability reports.

Maintenance carve-out: standard 72‑hour notice / 6 hours per month per region. As a concession for EU we will tighten to 96‑hour notice and reduce to 4 hours/month for EU region only, subject to the SOW.

I’ve attached: SLA_Template_v2_redlines.pdf (redlines called out), Monthly_Credit_Schedule_PineBridge.xlsx (numeric examples), and a short DocuSign commercial addendum link if you want to sign Option A quickly: https://app.docusign.com/s/78a2b1f

If you can confirm which option procurement prefers (A or B) and whether the EU carve-out tightening is required in the SOW, I’ll issue the final doc for signature and loop in Legal for a one‑page amendment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20‑minute call if that’s faster.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
